feature_name: Off-hours billing queue and billing reply macros
summary: Billing questions wait far longer for a first reply than other tickets, mostly outside the two billing agents' shifts. This routes off-hours billing tickets to a rota queue and gives rota agents reviewed reply macros, without new headcount.

statements.text: Billing tickets had a median first response of 31 hours versus 9 hours for other tickets in October 2026.
Billing was 38 percent of the 1240 October tickets.
Only 2 agents are trained on billing and both work weekday day shifts.
Billing questions arriving on Friday after 15:00 wait until Monday.
No new support headcount before 2027-01-01; the Q4 2026 tooling budget is 3000 USD.
Thin billing coverage outside weekday day shifts drives much of the billing delay.
Two non-billing agents can join an off-hours rota after a short training.
Whether slow billing replies lower customer satisfaction is unknown.
statements.resolution: Add a one-question satisfaction prompt on closed billing tickets during the pilot.

statements.text: How many billing questions a reply macro could answer is unknown.
statements.resolution: Tag a two-week sample of billing tickets by question type before writing macros.

objective.text: Bring billing first response close to other tickets this quarter without hiring.

key_results.metric: Median first response for billing tickets
Median first response for other tickets

segments.name: Customers with a billing question
segments.job: Get a billing question answered before it blocks a payment or renewal.

segments.name: Support agents without billing training
segments.job: Answer a billing ticket correctly without waiting for a billing specialist.
constraints: Rota shifts must fit current contracts.

value_propositions.why: A billing question often blocks paying or renewing.
value_propositions.before: Questions sent on Friday afternoon wait until Monday for one of 2 specialists.
value_propositions.how: Off-hours billing tickets go to a rota queue that is staffed every day.
value_propositions.after: They get a first reply within the same half day.
value_propositions.alternatives: Waiting, emailing again, or contacting sales.
value_propositions.statement: For customers with a billing question, the rota queue answers off-hours tickets the same day instead of after the weekend.

value_propositions.why: They see billing tickets they cannot answer and leave them in the queue.
value_propositions.before: They pass every billing ticket to the 2 trained agents.
value_propositions.how: Reviewed reply macros cover common billing questions.
value_propositions.after: They answer common billing questions themselves and escalate only the rest.
value_propositions.alternatives: Asking a specialist in chat or leaving the ticket.
value_propositions.statement: For agents without billing training, reviewed macros turn common billing tickets into ones they can close.

features.text: Route billing-tagged tickets created outside weekday day shifts to an off-hours billing queue.
Rota calendar that names the agent covering the off-hours billing queue each day.
Billing reply macros written and reviewed by the 2 billing-trained agents.

first_version.text: First set of reviewed billing macros.

later.text: Cross-training more agents, if the pilot misses its target.

non_goals.text: Automatic replies sent to customers without an agent.

release.timeframe: One sprint to configure, then a 28-day pilot.

constraints: No new headcount before the date in b-constraint.
Tooling spend stays within the Q4 budget in b-constraint.

acceptance_criteria.given: a billing-tagged ticket created on Friday at 16:00
acceptance_criteria.then: the ticket lands in the off-hours billing queue within 1 minute

acceptance_criteria.given: a billing-tagged ticket created on Tuesday at 10:00
acceptance_criteria.then: the ticket stays in the normal billing queue

trace.rationale: Daytime billing tickets keep going to the trained agents.

acceptance_criteria.given: the rota for the next 28 days
acceptance_criteria.then: every day has exactly 1 named agent for the off-hours billing queue
each macro has a recorded reviewer and review date

trace.rationale: Macros reach customers through agents, so a specialist signs off each one.

acceptance_criteria.then: billing median first response is 12 hours or less and other tickets stay at 12 hours or less

risks.text: Rota agents tire of off-hours shifts.
risks.mitigation: Rotate daily and cap each agent at two off-hours days a week.

risks.text: Seasonal billing volume changes hide the effect.
risks.mitigation: Compare against the same weeks of October and report volume next to the median.

risks.text: A macro gives a wrong billing answer.
risks.mitigation: Only reviewed macros are available; unclear cases are escalated.

handoff.notes: Helpdesk configuration only; the support lead accepts this draft before any change is made.

questions.text: Do off-hours rota shifts need extra pay or time off in lieu?

next_action.action: Support lead answers the rota-pay question and reviews this draft before configuration starts.
